goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and already remove Joao Pedro (about -19% on Chelsea's goals) plus Hato and Lacroix. They don't know Gittens is also out, so Chelsea may play without a recognised striker, with Estevao or Neto central, after scoring little in the games without Pedro; against Leeds' tight defence (eight conceded in ten) I keep a mild trim to about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Chelsea dominate the ball and their wide players (Neto, Chavarria, Palmer) drive most of their corners, while Leeds' back-three system is settled with Rodon back; nothing in the team news changes the width of either side, so about 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, already counting Michael Oliver (4.0 a game over 84 games, the league average) and Leeds' recent rise in bookings. Neither side has a suspension and the stakes are ordinary mid-table ones, so about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.4 shots, with Chelsea's recent dip in shot volume already in their momentum. Chelsea will have plenty of the ball and take speculative efforts even without a striker in form, so Gittens' absence affects quality more than volume; about 24.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. Chelsea managed only two on target at Sunderland despite 69% possession, and with Gittens now confirmed out as well as Pedro, their finishers are thin against a well-organised Leeds; a small trim to about 8.7.

analyst_view.overall: Chelsea are fifth under Xabi Alonso after losing 1-0 at Sunderland before the break, a game in which they had most of the ball but little end product; Leeds are ninth under Daniel Farke, two points behind, have conceded only eight league goals and beat Tottenham 1-0 last time out. Joao Pedro, Lacroix, Hato and Reece James are out and counted; Jamie Gittens (ankle) is also out but not on the numbers' list, and Sports Mole suggests Welbeck may be benched with Estevao or Neto used centrally beside Rogers and Palmer. Caicedo (illness) and Acheampong are available. Farke reports no injuries apart from the long-term absentee Mateo Joseph, with Stach and Okafor training all week. Michael Oliver referees, exactly at the league average for cards (counted).
